intro.headline: About Hestia Hearthwood
intro.sub: Storyteller, hearth-keeper, hopeless romantic for a well-built world.

paragraphs: Hestia Hearthwood is a name borrowed from the Greek goddess of the hearth — the keeper of home, warmth, and the fire that draws people together. It felt like the right name for someone who's always been happiest curled up in a cozy chair with a story, whether reading one or writing one.

I write romantasy and speculative fiction drawn to morally complicated characters, slow-burn tension, and worlds with real history behind them. My current project, Blood Memory, follows a reincarnated heroine caught in a centuries-old power struggle — equal parts gothic romance and political intrigue. Alongside it, I'm developing What the Roots Remember, a series set on a colonized world shaped by bloodline magic and the tension between nature and control.

When I'm not writing, I'm probably deep in a video game or curled up somewhere warm with a cup of tea, thinking about the next scene. Storytelling, for me, has always been about creating spaces people want to spend time in — whether that's a cozy living room or a five-hundred-year-old succession conflict.
